_comment: Phase 5 progression. Mining damage: a material yields 1 unit per `hp` damage. Tools deal `power` per swing every `interval` seconds, or `dps` while held (power tools). A tool (or machine) can only work material whose hardness <= its `max_hardness`.

tools.title: Rock Hammer
tools.desc: Grandpa's old hammer. Stone and coal only.

tools.title: Basic Pickaxe
tools.desc: Bites into stone and can crack iron.

tools.title: Reinforced Pickaxe
tools.desc: Steel-tipped. Every swing takes a real chunk.

tools.title: Power Drill
tools.desc: Hold to drill. Cuts copper veins.

stages.title: Manual Labor
stages.goal: Clear Grandpa's overgrown site: cut the weeds, break the rubble heaps and sell the stone.

stages.title: Better Tools
stages.goal: Buy a pickaxe at the upgrade board.

stages.title: First Employee
stages.goal: Hire your first helper at the office desk.

stages.title: Early Industrialization
stages.goal: Order a crusher, output storage and a front loader, and cut into the quarry face.

stages.title: Large-Scale Mining
stages.goal: Install a drilling rig, buy the dump truck and open up the first bench of the quarry.

stages.title: Deep Excavation
stages.goal: Buy the excavation permit, open the lower level and carve out the surface quarry.

hillside_face_01.title: Hillside Face
hillside_face_01._comment: Phase 6.1: first excavatable hillside, cut into the west rim. 6 columns deep (x, back wall at the west) by 12 wide (z). Only the east face is open; the other sides are solid hill, so rock is mined from the front and the cut deepens. Never resize an existing formation: saves store columns by count.

pit_band_01.title: Basin Bench
pit_band_01._comment: Phase 6.3b: a curved bench band inside the starting basin: 16 angular slices x 6 rings x 3 tiers (tops flush with the plateau). Only the inner ring is open; mining it pushes the face outward toward the basin wall. Angles are in the pit frame (0 deg = +x, -90 deg = toward the far wall).

fossil._comment: Phase 7.6: a fossil is buried in the gold bench of the lowest level. It is exposed only when the listed columns have really been mined out. The choice between the two buyers is final.
fossil.found_text:
The last of the stone falls away and there it is: a spine as long as a truck, ribs curving out of the rock like the hull of an old boat, and a skull with teeth the size of your hand. It is not stone. It is a skeleton, and it is enormous.

Nobody has stood here and seen this for millions of years.
toast: The lowest level has uncovered a huge fossil. Go and look (E).

collector.title: Sell to the collector
collector.pitch: A private collector, Mr. Vane, has heard rumours and offers $75,000 for the whole skeleton, crated and gone by the end of the week. It will hang in his private gallery.

scientist.title: Give it to the scientist
scientist.pitch: Dr. Evelyn Marsh of the university can pay only $2,000 towards the cost of the dig. But she will study it, put it on display for everyone, and her name for you will be 'the discoverer'.

fossil.confirm: This cannot be undone. Once you choose, the other buyer is gone for good.

results.collector: Mr. Vane's crew crates the bones and a truck takes them away. $75,000 lands in your account.
results.scientist: Dr. Marsh's team arrives the next morning, delighted. They cry a little. $2,000 and a promise: the university will keep in touch.

walter._comment: Phase 7.5: Walter is alive and retiring, not dead. Intro scene, timed visits and journal. Conditions: stage (id), quarry_level, cleaned (site cleanup done). Visits show once, in the morning/afternoon, when the player talks to him.

intro.speaker: GRANDPA WALTER
intro.text: There you are, kiddo. Come on over - I won't bite, I haven't got the teeth for it.

intro.speaker: GRANDPA WALTER
intro.text: Fifty years I've worked this quarry. My knees say that is forty-nine too many. The bank says the place is worth nothing, and the town says it never made a cent.

intro.speaker: GRANDPA WALTER
intro.text: They're wrong. There's good rock in these hills, and better rock under them. I just never had the machines - or the back - to dig it out.

intro.speaker: GRANDPA WALTER
intro.text: So I'm retiring, and I'm handing you the keys. The yard is overgrown and buried in rubble. Start small: take my old hammer, cut the weeds, break the heaps and sell the stone.

intro.speaker: GRANDPA WALTER
intro.text: The little house by the garage is yours too. Sleep there when the day is done - a rested miner is a careful miner.

intro.speaker: GRANDPA WALTER
intro.text: I'm only down the road. I'll come by now and then to see how the old place is doing. Don't let me catch you making a mess of it, hm?

lockbox.title: The lockbox
lockbox.text: Under the first rock I cleared there was Walter's old lockbox: a photo of the 1971 crew, notes about copper and gold below the north bench, and a savings bond.

handover.title: The handover
handover.text: Walter handed me the quarry and his old hammer. He is retiring, but he lives down the road and says he will look in on the place.

first_crew.title: A helping hand
first_crew.text: Walter says a quarry is a team sport: a good crew works while you rest. Pay them fairly and they will stay.

machines.title: Machines
machines.text: Walter admits he never owned a proper crusher or loader. 'Muscle gets you started. Machines get you finished.'

first_bench.title: The first bench
first_bench.text: The surface is opening up. Walter remembers the old crew standing on a floor much lower than this, and he says the stone down there looks different.

deep_dig.title: Going deep
deep_dig.text: Walter keeps looking at the lower levels. 'My father said the oldest things lie at the bottom. I never got far enough to see.'

big_dig.title: A real quarry
big_dig.text: Walter walked the rim for a long while. 'It's what I always wanted it to be.'

fossil_found.title: The thing in the rock
fossil_found.text: Something huge lay in the gold bench of the lowest level: a skeleton, ribs and spine and a skull full of teeth. Walter says his father always said so.

fossil_collector.title: Sold to the collector
fossil_collector.text: I sold the skeleton to Mr. Vane for $75,000. It is hanging in a private gallery now, where nobody will see it.

fossil_scientist.title: Given to the scientist
fossil_scientist.text: Dr. Marsh and her team took the skeleton for the university. I got $2,000 and the feeling of having done something right.

companion_egg.title: The egg
companion_egg.text: Dr. Marsh left an egg on the porch. It is warm and it moves a little. It should hatch in a couple of days.

companion_born.title: A new family member
companion_born.text: The egg hatched. I have a dinosaur. Walter says he has never seen anything like it.

companion_adult.title: All grown up
companion_adult.text: My dinosaur is fully grown. It can break rock with its tail.

visits.title: WALTER DROPS BY
lines: Heard you're thinking about hiring. Good. One pair of hands only goes so far.
Treat them well, learn what they're good at, and let them get on with it. A crew that is respected works twice as hard.

visits.title: WALTER DROPS BY
lines: A crusher and a loader! In my day we had a mule and a bad attitude.
Cut into the hillside from the front and work down, one bench at a time. And keep your crew fed with something to haul - idle machines eat money.

visits.title: WALTER DROPS BY
lines: You opened the first bench. I stood about there, forty years ago, and thought I'd never get any lower.
Go on down the ramp if you like. The coal and iron are better the deeper you go. And rock down there is older than anything in town.

visits.title: WALTER DROPS BY
lines: Copper and iron on level three. Now you are cutting where I only ever dreamed.
My father used to say the oldest things in this hill lie right at the bottom. Mind the walls, and take your time.

visits.title: WALTER DROPS BY
lines: Look at this. Look at all of it.
I thought I'd be too old to see it. I'm glad I wasn't. This is a real quarry now, kiddo.

visits.title: WALTER DROPS BY
lines: I heard. Is it true? Something is down in the rock at the bottom?
My father swore the oldest things in this hill lay at the very bottom. I laughed at him. Don't tell him.
Whoever you sell it to, kiddo, it's yours to decide. I'll back you either way. But think about what you want it to be.

visits.title: WALTER DROPS BY
lines: Seventy-five thousand. Well. That is a lot of money for some old bones.
I won't say I'd have done the same. I won't say I wouldn't have. It is your quarry now.

visits.title: WALTER DROPS BY
lines: Two thousand dollars and a whole university at your door. I like that.
You did right by it, kiddo. Whatever happens next, that skeleton is where it belongs.

visits.title: WALTER DROPS BY
lines: Is that an egg on the porch? Dr. Marsh left it for you?
Well, I never. Keep it warm and dry. I raised chickens once, how hard can it be?

visits.title: WALTER DROPS BY
lines: It hatched! Look at that little face.
You are going to have to feed it. Or at least be nice to it. It will follow you around the quarry like a puppy.

visits.title: WALTER DROPS BY
lines: Would you look at the size of it. And it can break rock with its tail!
In fifty years of working this quarry I never had a helper like that. Look after it, kiddo.

first_clear.title: GRANDPA'S LOCKBOX
first_clear.text:
Under the last of the rock sits a rusted lockbox. Inside:

- A faded photo of the crew in 1971, standing on this same floor.
- Mining records: 'Core sample, 3.5 m below the north bench: copper staining, trace gold.'
- A note: 'Didn't have the machines to go deeper. Maybe you will.'

There's also an old savings bond. It's still good.

story.intro2:
1. Left click swings your hammer. Cut the weeds and break the rubble heaps. The HUD counts the cleanup.

2. Carry the stone to the SALES booth and press E to sell it.

3. Spend your first money at the UPGRADE board outside the office: a pickaxe comes first.

4. When it gets dark (after 17:00) walk to the house by the garage and press E on the bed to sleep. Sleeping saves the game and starts a new morning.

5. Clean the whole site and Walt sends money, opens the hillside and the north gate.

cleanup._comment: Phase 6.2 tutorial: clear Grandpa's overgrown site (weeds and rubble heaps). Positions are fixed so saves can store what is left. Clearing everything unlocks the hillside and brings Walt's letter with the gift.
cleanup.gift_text:
Kiddo,

I heard you cleaned the old place up. I knew you would.

Now the real rock is open to you: the hillside behind the yard. Cut it from the front, one section at a time, and it will give up good stone.

I'm sending what I had put away. Spend it on a drill when you are ready. Machines are how we cut the big blocks.

- Grandpa Walt

pit_zone._comment: Phase 6.3a: the pit area north-east of the yard, entered through a gate in the cliff ring. Local frame: origin at the gate, -Z points out of the quarry. The yard keeps its coordinates.

world._comment: Phase 7.1. The industrial hub is the yard inside the cliff ring (x -23.5..23.5, z -6..23.5, plus the east expansion); it is the permanent business area and is never excavated. The main quarry is the pit zone reached through the north-east gate (see pit_zone), where all four levels are cut.

quarry_levels._comment: Four levels of ONE continuous quarry (Phase 7.2). 'formations' are cut in that level; 'unlock' is the share of the PREVIOUS level that must be excavated before the level's rock can be mined (the shell, ramp and walls are always there, under the flush columns). 'pit' (pit frame): rect = [x0, z0, x1, z1] of the whole pit including its ramp strip on the west side; ramp_w = width of that strip; the ramp runs along z from the south end (z1, previous floor) down to the north end (z0, this floor); the columns fill the rest of the rectangle.
quarry_levels.title: Surface Operations

companion._comment: Phase 7.7: Dr. Marsh's team leaves the egg (scientist route only). Days are in-game days. Stages: egg -> hatchling -> juvenile -> adult. Tail smash: damage per hit and the hardest rock the companion can break (the same hardness rule as the player's tools).
companion.arrival_text: A crate sits on the porch with a note: 'Keep it warm and dry. It should hatch in a couple of days. Please look after it. - Dr. Evelyn Marsh'. Inside is an egg the size of a watermelon, warm to the touch.
companion.hatch_text: The egg cracks, wobbles, and a small, wet, very serious head pokes out. It looks at you and decides you are its family.
companion.adult_text: %s has grown into a full-size dinosaur. It can smash open hard rock with its tail now.
companion.juvenile_text: %s is growing fast. It is big enough to smash soft rock with its tail now (press T while looking at rock).
